As written, eight present-tense currency sites in the very files the entry names stay ungoverned: a later hunt applying the rule literally cannot classify 'Current G09 GATE leftover-join is g09 leftover-join.v11' as custody-at-recording, and the version-number reading D-293 Decision 4 says stands until this entry is adopted would still re-flag permission leftover-join.v12 and packaging leftover-join.v4 on those sentences. No standing conclusion changes - the pair set and the partition equalities are unchanged - which is why this is SHOULD-FIX and not MUST-FIX.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 3 SHOULD-FIX. Everything load-bearing reproduces from bytes: all ten citation rows (27 sites, verbatim first sites, named obligation ids, byte-identical partitions, equal projections), all eleven supersession rows, the exactly-eight/exactly-ten claim across all 37 current joins, every recording heading, every precedent quotation (D-269, D-276, D-278, D-281, D-282, D-285, D-288), the branch enumeration, the D-293 Decision 4 grant, and the live file-08 remasurement. The three defects are in the rule text itself: SF1 the citation grammar misses two present-tense currency forms present at eight pair-sites in the named files (inverted 'Current ... is X vN'; 'Cite X vN as the current'); SF2 Decision 1 enumerates three of four directions while a GATE-to-GATE citation (g25 v5 -> g23 v8) exists in current bytes; SF3 'the occupancy-stale class recorded from D-261 through D-287' starts eleven entries late (D-250 through D-260 record the same class, four of them cited by the draft) and spans CONTESTED D-272. All three are wording fixes; no standing conclusion, count of pairs, partition, or readiness number changes.
